title: Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 (No. 38, 2026), as made
used_for: Assent date; commencement rule (s 2) and the Register's commencement column; definitions of digital token, DAP, TCP, wrapped token and public digital token infrastructure (ss 761GB, 761GC, 761GD, 765E, 9E); constitutionally-covered corporation rule (s 766M); licensee obligations (ss 912BB to 912BH); DAP/TCP Guide, voting policy and communications (ss 1020AN to 1020AR); design and distribution trigger (s 994B); fundraising rules (ss 741A, 741B); exemptions (ss 9 (me), (mf), 765A(1), 766A(3), 768A(2)(ha), 911A(2)(ja), (jb), 911A(4B)); managed investment scheme carve-outs (s 9 (mc), (md)); ministerial powers (ss 767B, 767C, 768B, 768C, 912BH); transitional rules (ss 1730 to 1733).

title: Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act (The Constitution), section 51(xx)
used_for: Section 51(xx): "Foreign corporations, and trading or financial corporations formed within the limits of the Commonwealth". Used to explain the Act's term "constitutionally-covered corporation".

title: Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Bill 2025: bill homepage and progress
used_for: Introduced 26 November 2025; passed the House 4 February 2026; introduced in the Senate and referred to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee 5 February 2026; committee report 16 March 2026; finally passed both Houses 1 April 2026; assent 8 April 2026. Also links the Explanatory Memorandum and Bills Digest.

title: New digital asset laws to unlock innovation and safeguard investment (joint media release)
publisher: Treasurer and Minister for Financial Services
used_for: Why the law was introduced (client assets held without financial law safeguards; overseas collapses); two new financial products; AFSL core obligations; small-platform exemption described as under $5,000 per customer and under $10 million in yearly transactions.

title: ASIC's roadmap for digital assets law reform implementation
used_for: 18-month implementation timeline; ASIC's plan to consult on asset-holding standards, transactional and settlement standards and financial requirements; indicative topics (holding on trust, segregation, record keeping, reconciliation, withdrawal rights); at the time, stated commencement of 9 April 2027.

title: Deadline looms for digital asset businesses to apply for a licence
used_for: INFO 225 no-action position (then due to end 30 June 2026) concerns licensing under existing law; penalties for unlicensed conduct; Act passed 1 April 2026; at the time, stated commencement of 9 April 2027.

title: ASIC extends no-action position for digital asset businesses to 30 September 2026
used_for: Extension of the sector-wide INFO 225 no-action position from 30 June 2026 to 30 September 2026, and its expanded scope.

title: 26-245MR ASIC consults on implementation of new digital asset laws
used_for: New laws commence 8 April 2027; CP 392 contents; consultation closes 5pm AEDT 27 November 2026; "same activity, same risk, same regulatory outcome"; no-action deadline extended to 30 September 2026; ASIC recorded over 140 digital asset-related applications.

title: Consultation Paper 392 Digital asset law reform implementation: Proposed standards and guidance
used_for: Next steps timeline (feedback by 27 November 2026; final instruments and guidance March 2027; commencement and applications open 8 April 2027; transition window closes 7 October 2027); purpose of the Act (paras 2 to 5); licensing from 8 October 2027 (para 39); related services need licensing (para 41); continue operating if applied by deadline (para 45); proposed new exemptions (para 38); payments reforms and tokenised stored value facilities (paras 6 and 7).

title: Draft Regulatory Guide 000 Digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms (Attachment 1 to CP 392)
used_for: A DAP or TCP is a financial product separate from assets held through it (RG 000.20 to 000.21); INFO 225 to be updated on public digital token infrastructure (RG 000.22 note); not every tokenisation arrangement is a TCP and native tokenised fund units are generally a managed investment scheme (RG 000.33 note, RG 000.35 note); DAP scope and technology-provider carve-out (RG 000.36 to 000.41); wrapped token treatment (RG 000.48); managed investment scheme interaction (RG 000.49 to 000.53); custodial staking (RG 000.58 to 000.59); markets and CS facilities prevail (RG 000.60 to 000.62); exemptions do not stop a facility being a DAP or TCP, and Table 3 of key exemptions (RG 000.75 to 000.77); TMD needed where a DAP/TCP Guide is required (Section D table).

title: Tokeniser: home page and FAQ
used_for: Tokeniser's own description: SaaS for fund administration and investor portals, operating on Redbelly Network; "Products issued through Tokeniser operate under an Asset Issuer's existing licensing"; eligibility (identity, KYC, AML, CTF, wholesale and sophisticated investor tests, TMD) programmed into each asset and checked on every transfer.

title: Tokeniser: Our technology
used_for: Tokeniser's statements that Redbelly is designed to meet the three statutory tests for public digital token infrastructure and to sit outside markets, clearing and settlement, and custody licensing; deterministic finality; TMD enforced at point of transfer.

title: Tokeniser: Protocol finance
used_for: Tokeniser's view that automated market maker liquidity, lending and settlement sit in an exempt protocol layer, citing the Explanatory Memorandum; its own guardrails, including that a protocol with a controlling foundation, admin key or privileged role needs to evidence its design against s 9E(2)(c).

title: How does Tokeniser handle investor compliance? (Knowledge Hub)
used_for: KYC/AML and investor classification before wallet activation; compliance parameters enforced at transfer; checks and rejections recorded on-chain and in a compliance log; fund manager remains responsible for configuration and remains the AML/CTF reporting entity.

title: What is self-custodial asset administration? (Knowledge Hub)
used_for: Tokeniser says it does not hold the private key (the investor or a designated key manager does) and provides key management and recovery options.

title: Tokeniser: About us
used_for: Tokeniser describes itself as a Redbelly Network project, and lists a division of responsibility in which IQ-EQ provides trust, registry, fund administration, and licence and service.

title: Asset tokenisation on Redbelly Network
used_for: Redbelly's statements that eligibility is enforced at the point of trade using verifiable credentials and that AML, CTF and Travel Rule requirements can be applied as needed.

title: Receptor (ID protocol), Redbelly Network technical documentation
used_for: Receptor is Redbelly's native digital identity and verifiable credential protocol; it facilitates network access; issuers who provide network access are accredited by Redbelly; built on the W3C verifiable credential data model.

title: Eligibility Kit overview, Redbelly Network technical documentation
used_for: Toolkit for real-world asset issuers to verify investor eligibility using zero-knowledge proofs without the user revealing sensitive personal data.

title: Configure eligibility criteria, Redbelly Network technical documentation
used_for: Eligibility criteria are written as queries over credentials (for example country, age, AML status); supported credential types include AMLCTFCredential and AUSophisticatedWholesaleInvestorCredential; revocation checks should stay on in production.

title: Individual onboarding overview, Redbelly Network technical documentation
used_for: Individual onboarding to gain access to the Redbelly Network includes wallet authentication, KYC verification and on-chain permission setup.

title: Business onboarding overview, Redbelly Network technical documentation
used_for: Business onboarding (KYB) is provided by Averer and deploys an on-chain Business Identifier contract that can delegate access to company wallets.

title: Network nodes, Redbelly Vine developer portal
used_for: Node operators are described as successful applicants who receive an invitation to run a node.

title: Network reconfiguration, Redbelly Vine developer portal
used_for: Governor and candidate nodes; governors are rotated; governors must notify Redbelly of planned downtime and may be demoted or replaced under the governance rules.

title: Rewards and incentives, Redbelly Vine developer portal
used_for: Each node operator must stake RBNT to be eligible to participate in Mainnet; Redbelly reserves the right to slash the stake of misbehaving participants.
